newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mozambique sounds early warning on drought threat.
newsitem.headline: Mozambique sounds early warning on drought threat.

text.p: The southern African nation of Mozambique could face a drought in the coming crop season, a weather expert said on Wednesday.
"After two good years there is now a possibility of drought," Antonio Olivares, chief of an early warning unit at the Agriculture Ministry, told Reuters.
Olivares said it was too early give an accurate prediction but the "southern oscillation index" -- an atmospheric indicator linked to the EL Nino weather phenomenon -- suggested poor rains.
A more accurate picture will emerge in late September. The El Nino effect is associated with with drought in Southern Africa and Australia.
"Until now the index is negative but it could change. The September index will correlate with December and January, which are the critical months in Mozambique," Olivares said.

Maize would be the main affected crop if drought does come. The agriculture ministry says it has already started distributing seeds for hardy crops such as sorghum and cow-pea in anticipation of a drought.
Mozambique suffered devastating droughts in the early 1980s and 1990s but in 1997 had such a good harvest that it was able to export some of its maize.

Last month, a wide range of Southern African weather and agricultural experts voiced concern about the early build-up of an El Nino, saying it could spark a devastating drought in the region next year.

The Southern African Development Community's Food Security Unit forecast in June that 1996/97 maize production might drop 16 percent to 17,142 million tonnes from the previous season, attributing this to floods in some states and drought in others.
